You are given a center-based facility location optimization problem.

Problem description:
There is a set of locations. Each location represents a demand point, and any location may also be opened as a service center.
The travel distance between every ordered pair of locations is given (as pairs).
Every location must be served by exactly one opened service center.

Decision variables:
- Select a fixed number of locations to open as service centers (the required number is specified in the input).
- Assign every location to exactly one opened service center.

Constraints:
- Each location must be assigned to exactly one service center.
- A location can only be assigned to a service center that is opened.

Objective:
Minimize the worst-case service distance, defined as the maximum travel distance between any location and the service center it is assigned to.

You will receive the problem instance in the following format:
{{INSTANCE_INPUT}}

Your task is to choose which locations to open as service centers and how to assign all locations to them, so that the maximum assignment distance is minimized.

If multiple optimal solutions exist, you may return any one of them.

Reply using exactly the following JSON structure (no extra keys, no explanations):
```json
{
  "solution": {
    "selected": [<location_to_open>, <location_to_open>, ...],
    "assignments": [<chosen_open_location>, <chosen_open_location>, ...]
  }
}
```
Here, `selected` is the list of locations chosen to host service centers.
The `assignments` list has the same length and order as the locations described in the input; the i-th entry specifies which opened location serves location i.
All identifiers must match exactly those used in the input, and every assignment must refer to one of the locations listed in `selected`.
**Do not include explanations or any extra keys.**

contexts.text: [BASELINE] Canonical task wording.

As the city mobility planner, pick a predetermined number of bike parking hubs from the candidate sites so that every street intersection is assigned to a single opened hub and the longest walking distance any cyclist must cover is kept as small as possible.

Help the regional health coordinator select a fixed number of pop up vaccination locations among possible venues, assign each neighborhood to a single opened location, and aim to minimize the furthest travel time any resident faces.

As a retail network manager, choose a specified number of pickup lockers at available addresses, link every customer address to a single opened locker, and design the choices to reduce the maximum trip distance customers need to travel.

Advise the school transport officer to establish a predetermined quantity of bus stop sites from proposed spots, allocate each household to a single opened stop, and make the worst case walking distance from house to stop as small as possible.

Task the utility planner with opening a fixed number of water refill stations among candidate points, assign every block to a single opened station, and keep the greatest distance anyone travels to their assigned station minimized.

global_fields.name: num_open

pair_item_fields.name: distance

global_fields.name: num_nodes

global_fields.name: num_open

global_fields.name: num_nodes

global_fields.scenario_description: The exact number of water refill kiosks the team must select and open. The solver must pick this many sites to minimize the maximum walk distance.

global_fields.name: nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: Ordered list of identifiers (names or IDs) for each candidate park location / picnic area referenced in the instance. These IDs index the locations that can host kiosks and that must be assigned to an opened kiosk.

pair_item_fields.name: from_id
pair_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the starting location for this distance entry — the picnic area (or candidate site) a visitor would walk from when measuring distance to another location.

pair_item_fields.name: to_id
pair_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the target location for this distance entry — the site (potential kiosk or other park spot) being measured to from the origin.

pair_item_fields.name: distance
pair_item_fields.scenario_description: The numeric walking distance along park paths between the origin and destination locations. These distances are used to assign picnic areas to opened kiosks and to evaluate the maximum walk any visitor must take.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of distinct plaza locations under consideration — each is an identifier for a point in the concert area that can represent a crowd cluster location and/or a potential food-stall site.

global_fields.name: num_open
global_fields.scenario_description: How many food stalls may be opened (the fixed number p). You must choose this many candidate spots to operate as service points.

global_fields.name: nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: A list of identifiers for every plaza location referenced in the instance. These IDs correspond to spots where crowds might gather and where stalls could be placed; every crowd location must be assigned to one of the opened stall locations.

pair_item_fields.name: from_id
pair_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the origin location for the distance pair — typically the location of a crowd group (or a plaza point) whose travel to a stall is being measured.

pair_item_fields.name: to_id
pair_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the destination location for the distance pair — typically a candidate food-stall spot being considered as the assigned service point for the origin.

pair_item_fields.name: distance
pair_item_fields.scenario_description: The travel distance along plaza paths from the origin to the destination (e.g., meters or other consistent units). This value is used to compute how far a crowd at the origin would walk if assigned to the stall at the destination.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of distinct locations in this instance (every place that appears in the distance matrix). This count includes candidate box sites and delivery addresses and determines the size of the nodes list and distance data.

global_fields.name: num_open
global_fields.scenario_description: The fixed number of rural collection boxes the planners must select from the candidate sites. Exactly this many sites will be opened as service points.

global_fields.name: nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: An ordered list of identifiers for all locations referenced in the instance (each house/delivery point and each candidate box site). These identifiers index the distance pairs and are used when assigning each delivery point to one opened box.

pair_item_fields.name: from_id
pair_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the first location in a distance record (the source in the ordered pair). This may be a delivery address or a candidate site and is used together with to_id to specify a measured travel distance.

pair_item_fields.name: to_id
pair_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the second location in a distance record (the target in the ordered pair). Paired with from_id to identify the two locations between which the travel distance was measured.

pair_item_fields.name: distance
pair_item_fields.scenario_description: The measured travel distance between the origin_location_id and destination_location_id along the road network (the distance a resident would travel between those two points). These values are used to compute each delivery point's distance to candidate/opened boxes and to evaluate the maximum assigned travel distance.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of candidate locations (the count of all neighborhood clusters and potential mobile book stop sites considered when planning stops).

global_fields.name: num_open
global_fields.scenario_description: The fixed number of mobile book stops that must be selected/opened for the plan.

global_fields.name: nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: An ordered list of identifiers for every candidate location (each neighborhood cluster and potential stop). These IDs are used when assigning each neighborhood to exactly one opened stop.

pair_item_fields.name: from_id
pair_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the source location in this distance record (the neighborhood cluster or location from which travel is measured).

pair_item_fields.name: to_id
pair_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the target location in this distance record (the potential mobile stop or other location to which travel is measured).

pair_item_fields.name: distance
pair_item_fields.scenario_description: The travel distance between the source and target locations (same units throughout). This value is used to determine how far a neighborhood would have to go if assigned to that candidate stop when minimizing the maximum assigned travel distance.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total count of distinct locations in the camping area that appear in the instance — these are the candidate spots where a restroom can be opened and the campsites that must be assigned (i.e., the number of site identifiers listed).

global_fields.name: num_open
global_fields.scenario_description: How many sanitation stations (restrooms) the planners must choose to open from the available locations. This is the fixed number of service points the solution must place.

global_fields.name: nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The ordered list of identifiers for every spot in the instance (each campsite and each candidate restroom location). Each id corresponds to one node for which distances to other nodes are provided.

pair_item_fields.name: from_id
pair_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the origin site for this distance measurement — the starting location (e.g., a campsite or candidate restroom) from which the walk to another site is measured.

pair_item_fields.name: to_id
pair_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the destination site for this distance measurement — the target location (e.g., a candidate restroom or campsite) to which the walk from the origin is measured.

pair_item_fields.name: distance
pair_item_fields.scenario_description: The measured walking distance between the two listed sites (from_site_id to to_site_id). This is the value used to assign campsites to opened restrooms and to evaluate the maximum walk any camper must take.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of candidate sites on campus (every dorm and classroom area) that are considered in the instance — i.e., the number of locations that might host or be assigned to a vending machine.

global_fields.name: num_open
global_fields.scenario_description: The fixed number of vending machines you must install (the number of service points that will be opened).

global_fields.name: nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: An ordered list of the identifiers for each dorm or classroom area in the instance. Each identifier names a candidate location that can either host a vending machine or be assigned to one.

pair_item_fields.name: from_id
pair_item_fields.scenario_description: The identifier of the source location for a pairwise walking distance — the dorm or classroom from which the distance to another location is measured (used when considering assigning this site to a vending machine at another site).

pair_item_fields.name: to_id
pair_item_fields.scenario_description: The identifier of the target location for a pairwise walking distance — the dorm or classroom or candidate machine site that is the destination of the measured walk.

pair_item_fields.name: distance
pair_item_fields.scenario_description: The walking distance (e.g., meters or minutes) from the origin location to the destination location. This value is used to determine assignment costs and to compute the objective (the maximum distance anyone must walk to their assigned vending machine).

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: Total count of distinct candidate places in the district. Each identifier in 'location_ids' represents a hamlet (and a possible kiosk site); this number is the size of that list.

global_fields.name: num_open
global_fields.scenario_description: The fixed number of potable-water kiosks that must be opened across the region — the exact number of service points you are allowed to place.

global_fields.name: nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The list of identifiers (names or IDs) for every candidate location/hamlet. Every entry here must be assigned to exactly one opened kiosk.

pair_item_fields.name: from_id
pair_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the source location in this distance pair (the hamlet or site from which travel is measured).

pair_item_fields.name: to_id
pair_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the destination location in this distance pair (the potential kiosk site being measured to from 'from_location_id').

pair_item_fields.name: distance
pair_item_fields.scenario_description: The travel distance between the two locations listed (from_location_id → to_location_id). These distances determine how far a hamlet would travel to an assigned kiosk and are used to evaluate the worst-case travel distance.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total count of locations in the instance — every candidate dock site and every popular origin point that appears in the neighborhood map. This is the number of entries expected in the nodes list.

global_fields.name: num_open
global_fields.scenario_description: The fixed number of docking stations you must choose to operate (the k service points). These are the docks that will be opened and to which every origin will be assigned.

global_fields.name: nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: A list of identifiers for every location in the scenario (each candidate dock site and popular origin point). Each identifier is referenced by the pairwise distance records and is used when assigning origins to open docks.

pair_item_fields.name: from_id
pair_item_fields.scenario_description: The identifier of the starting location for this distance record (may be a potential dock or an origin). Combined with to_id, it names the ordered pair whose travel distance is given.

pair_item_fields.name: to_id
pair_item_fields.scenario_description: The identifier of the ending location for this distance record (may be a potential dock or an origin). Together with from_id, it identifies which two locations the walking distance measures.

pair_item_fields.name: distance
pair_item_fields.scenario_description: The travel distance between the source_location_id and target_location_id. Use these distances to determine how far someone would walk if assigned to a particular open dock; the objective minimizes the maximum such walking_distance over all assignments.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of distinct place identifiers referenced in this instance — i.e., the count of all mapped locations appearing in the input (this can include approved donation‑bin spots and apartment clusters used in the distance matrix).

global_fields.name: num_open
global_fields.scenario_description: How many donation bins you are required to open (the fixed number of approved bin locations to choose).

global_fields.name: nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The list of all location identifiers used in the instance. Each identifier names a place referenced in the distance data (approved bin spots and/or apartment cluster locations) that can appear as a source or target in distance pairs.

pair_item_fields.name: from_id
pair_item_fields.scenario_description: The identifier of the origin location for this distance entry (the starting place for the measured walk, e.g., an apartment cluster or a candidate bin spot).

pair_item_fields.name: to_id
pair_item_fields.scenario_description: The identifier of the destination location for this distance entry (the target place for the measured walk, typically a candidate donation‑bin spot or an apartment cluster).

pair_item_fields.name: distance
pair_item_fields.scenario_description: The walking distance between the origin and destination in this row — the travel cost donors would incur going from from_id to to_id; these distances are used to assign each apartment cluster to an opened bin and to evaluate the maximum (worst) assigned distance.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: Total count of locations listed in the instance — every identifier that can act as a potential pop-up venue or represents a neighborhood customer cluster. This is the size of the set from which booths are selected and to which clusters are assigned.

global_fields.name: num_open
global_fields.scenario_description: How many temporary pop-up booths must be opened (the fixed number of venues to select from the candidate locations).

global_fields.name: nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: Ordered list of the identifiers for all locations in the instance. Each id refers to a candidate venue or a neighborhood cluster that must be assigned to one opened booth.

pair_item_fields.name: from_id
pair_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the source location for a distance entry — refers to a candidate venue or neighborhood cluster used to describe travel from this location to another.

pair_item_fields.name: to_id
pair_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the target location for a distance entry — refers to the location reached from the source location in this distance record.

pair_item_fields.name: distance
pair_item_fields.scenario_description: Travel distance (e.g., walking distance) between the two specified locations. These distances are used to determine how far a neighborhood would have to travel to its assigned open booth and to evaluate the maximum (worst-case) assignment distance.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: Total count of candidate spots (aisles or specific store locations) considered for placing pickup counters; equals the number of location identifiers in the map.

global_fields.name: num_open
global_fields.scenario_description: The fixed number of pickup counters the store must open among the candidate spots; this many locations will be selected as service points.

global_fields.name: nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: List of all location identifiers for the store layout (each id denotes an aisle or product-area location). Each id is a potential counter site and also a demand point that must be assigned to exactly one opened counter.

pair_item_fields.name: from_id
pair_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the origin spot for a measured shopper walk (the product area or aisle customers start from when going to a counter).

pair_item_fields.name: to_id
pair_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the destination spot for a measured shopper walk (the candidate or opened pickup counter location being reached).

pair_item_fields.name: distance
pair_item_fields.scenario_description: Precomputed walking distance between the from_spot_id and to_spot_id along store aisles; used to determine how far customers assigned from one spot must walk to a chosen counter (the metric the p-center objective minimizes).

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total count of candidate locations in the terminal (every gate and every baggage carousel location considered in the layout). This is the number of distinct IDs in the nodes list from which carousels may be chosen and gates will be assigned.

global_fields.name: num_open
global_fields.scenario_description: The fixed number of baggage claim carousels you must turn on (the number of service points to open). Every arriving gate will be assigned to one of these activated carousels.

global_fields.name: nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: An ordered list of the identifiers for all terminal locations in the instance — including gate identifiers and carousel identifiers. These IDs are the universe from which you pick which carousel locations to activate and to which you refer distances.

pair_item_fields.name: from_id
pair_item_fields.scenario_description: The identifier of the origin location for this distance measurement. In the assignment context this will typically be a gate (the passenger start), but entries may use any location ID as the distance source.

pair_item_fields.name: to_id
pair_item_fields.scenario_description: The identifier of the destination location for this distance measurement. When assigning a gate to an activated carousel, use the distance from the gate (origin) to that carousel (destination).

pair_item_fields.name: distance
pair_item_fields.scenario_description: The passenger walking distance between the origin and destination location (in the units given by the instance). These pairwise distances are used to compute each gate's assigned walk and the overall maximum walk you aim to minimize.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of candidate trail intersections (including trailheads) where a water fountain could be placed; equals the size of the distance matrix and the total count of locations that must be assigned to an opened fountain.

global_fields.name: num_open
global_fields.scenario_description: The fixed number of water fountains that must be installed (i.e., how many of the candidate intersections will be chosen as open service points).

global_fields.name: nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: An ordered list of identifiers (labels or IDs) for every candidate intersection/trailhead in the instance; these IDs are used as the 'from' and 'to' references in the distance records and for assigning each location to exactly one open fountain.

pair_item_fields.name: from_id
pair_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the origin intersection for this distance record — the trailhead or intersection from which the walking distance is measured toward another intersection.

pair_item_fields.name: to_id
pair_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the destination intersection for this distance record — the intersection (possible fountain location) to which the walking distance from the source is given.

pair_item_fields.name: distance
pair_item_fields.scenario_description: The measured walking distance along trails from the source intersection to the target intersection; used to assign each trailhead to an open fountain and to compute the maximum assigned distance that the solution seeks to minimize.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of candidate curb-side spots (city curb slots) considered for pickup zones. This is the size of the set of all locations in the instance.

global_fields.name: num_open
global_fields.scenario_description: How many pickup zones (service points) the planner must open among the curb slots. Exactly this many slots will be chosen as active pickup zones.

global_fields.name: nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The list of identifiers for each curb-side spot (each rider area / candidate location). These IDs index the rows/columns of the travel-time table and are the elements that must be assigned to opened pickup zones.

pair_item_fields.name: from_id
pair_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the source curb slot in a pairwise travel-time entry: the rider area or curb slot from which travel to another slot is measured.

pair_item_fields.name: to_id
pair_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the target curb slot in a pairwise travel-time entry: the pickup zone or curb slot to which travel from the source is measured.

pair_item_fields.name: distance
pair_item_fields.scenario_description: The travel time (distance) from the origin curb slot to the destination curb slot, using the same time/distance units provided in the instance. These pairwise times form the complete matrix used to evaluate assignment distances.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of dorm-floor locations under consideration. Each listed location represents a resident demand point and a candidate site where a laundry room could be opened.

global_fields.name: num_open
global_fields.scenario_description: How many laundry rooms the housing office must choose to operate. Exactly this many locations will be opened as service points.

global_fields.name: nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: An ordered list of identifiers (room numbers or location codes) for every dorm location in the instance. Every identifier corresponds to a resident room that must be assigned to one opened laundry room.

pair_item_fields.name: from_id
pair_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the source dorm location in this distance pair — typically the resident room whose walk to a laundry is being measured.

pair_item_fields.name: to_id
pair_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the target dorm location in this distance pair — typically the candidate laundry site (or another room) used to record the walk between the two locations.

pair_item_fields.name: distance
pair_item_fields.scenario_description: The measured walking distance from from_location_id to to_location_id according to the dorm-floor map. These distances are used to assign every resident to an opened laundry and to evaluate the maximum walk any resident must take.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of neighborhood locations that are candidates for placing a library book drop box. This is the size of the set of sites among which you must choose.

global_fields.name: num_open
global_fields.scenario_description: The fixed number of book drop boxes the library will open. Exactly this many candidate sites must be selected as active drop-box locations.

global_fields.name: nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: An ordered list of identifiers (names or codes) for each neighborhood location considered as a potential drop-box site; every identifier corresponds to one candidate location.

pair_item_fields.name: from_id
pair_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the source location in a pairwise distance entry — the patron area or neighborhood location from which distance to another site is measured and that will be assigned to an opened drop box.

pair_item_fields.name: to_id
pair_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the target location in a pairwise distance entry — the candidate neighborhood site (potential drop box) to which the origin area’s travel distance is given.

pair_item_fields.name: distance
pair_item_fields.scenario_description: The travel distance or time between the origin area and the destination site. These distances (given for every ordered pair) are used to assign each area to one opened drop box and to evaluate the maximum assigned travel distance.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total count of roadside candidate locations where an emergency kit could be placed. This tells the solver how many locations must be considered and matches the length of the 'nodes' list.

global_fields.name: num_open
global_fields.scenario_description: The fixed number of emergency kit stations the safety office must open. The solver must choose exactly this many locations from the candidates as opened kit sites.

global_fields.name: nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: An ordered list of identifiers for every roadside location in the instance (candidate kit sites and demand points). Each identifier is used to reference locations when specifying pairwise travel distances and when assigning locations to opened kit stations.

pair_item_fields.name: from_id
pair_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the origin roadside location for this distance entry. Used together with 'to_id' to specify the travel distance from one location to another in the pairwise distance data.

pair_item_fields.name: to_id
pair_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the destination roadside location for this distance entry. Paired with 'from_id' to define the travel distance that will be used to compute assignment costs and the maximum assigned travel distance.

pair_item_fields.name: distance
pair_item_fields.scenario_description: The travel distance from the location named by 'from_id' to the location named by 'to_id' (in the same units for all entries). These distances determine how far drivers would travel to reach an assigned kit and are used to evaluate the worst-case (maximum) assignment distance.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of data-center racks considered in this instance. Each rack is a candidate location for hosting a backup server and also represents an application-server location that must be assigned to one opened backup.

global_fields.name: num_open
global_fields.scenario_description: The fixed number of backup servers the administrator must deploy — i.e., how many racks must be selected to host backups.

global_fields.name: nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: An ordered list of identifiers for every rack in the instance. Each identifier names a candidate rack that may host a backup and that must be assigned to exactly one opened backup.

pair_item_fields.name: from_id
pair_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the source rack (the rack where an application server sits and will be assigned to a backup).

pair_item_fields.name: to_id
pair_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the target rack (a candidate rack that could host a backup server to which the source rack might be assigned).

pair_item_fields.name: distance
pair_item_fields.scenario_description: Measured communication latency from the source rack to the target rack (for example, in milliseconds). These pairwise latencies are used to determine assignment costs and to evaluate the maximum (worst-case) latency that the solution seeks to minimize.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of candidate street corners in the neighborhood. Each corner is both a potential mailbox location and a delivery area that must be assigned to exactly one opened mailbox; use this to know how many node IDs appear in the nodes list.

global_fields.name: num_open
global_fields.scenario_description: Exact number of public mail drop boxes the planner must install. The solution must choose exactly this many corners from the candidates as opened service points.

global_fields.name: nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: List of identifiers for each street corner (node) in the instance. Each ID names a candidate mailbox site and a delivery area that will be assigned to one opened mailbox; these IDs are referenced by the distance records.

pair_item_fields.name: from_id
pair_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the source corner (the delivery area origin) in a distance record. This ID must match one of the entries in corner_ids and indicates the location from which walking distance to a candidate box is measured.

pair_item_fields.name: to_id
pair_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the target corner (the candidate mailbox location) in a distance record. This ID must match one of the entries in corner_ids and indicates the destination corner whose distance from the source is given.

pair_item_fields.name: distance
pair_item_fields.scenario_description: Walking distance from the source corner to the target corner as measured for the instance (in the units provided, e.g., meters or minutes). These distances are used to assign each delivery area to an opened box and to compute the maximum assigned walking distance that the planner seeks to minimize.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of playing fields in the tournament. Each field is both a team location and a candidate site where a water station can be placed; this equals the length of the 'field_ids' list.

global_fields.name: num_open
global_fields.scenario_description: How many water stations (water carts) you must open among the playing fields. You will choose exactly this many fields to host stations.

global_fields.name: nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: List of identifiers for all playing fields. Each identifier denotes a team location and a potential station site that can be opened and assigned teams.

pair_item_fields.name: from_id
pair_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the source playing field in a pair; represents the team's location when measuring the walk to a candidate station.

pair_item_fields.name: to_id
pair_item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the target playing field in a pair; represents the candidate station location the team at 'from_field_id' would walk to.

pair_item_fields.name: distance
pair_item_fields.scenario_description: Walking distance between the two fields (from 'from_field_id' to 'to_field_id'). These pairwise distances are used to assign each team to one opened station and to evaluate the maximum assigned walk length to be minimized.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of bike-path junctions being considered as candidate locations for repair stands; equals the count of identifiers in the junction list.

global_fields.name: num_open
global_fields.scenario_description: The fixed number of bicycle repair stands the planner must place among the junctions; this many junctions will be chosen to host open stands.

global_fields.name: nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: An ordered list of unique identifiers for every junction (each a common origin or destination) that can host a repair stand or be assigned to one; these IDs are referenced by the distance entries.

pair_item_fields.name: from_id
pair_item_fields.scenario_description: The identifier of the starting junction for this distance record; must match one of the junction_ids and represents one endpoint of the ride distance measurement.

pair_item_fields.name: to_id
pair_item_fields.scenario_description: The identifier of the ending junction for this distance record; must match one of the junction_ids and represents the other endpoint of the ride distance measurement.

pair_item_fields.name: distance
pair_item_fields.scenario_description: The bicycle ride distance along the path network from origin_junction to destination_junction (e.g., meters or kilometers); used to evaluate how far a cyclist would travel when assigned to a particular open repair stand.
